entities.summary: Išhtup-Išar was a king (Lugal) of the second Mariote kingdom, ruling from circa 1770 to 1750 BCE. His name was traditionally read as Išhtup-šar, but was later adapted to Ishtup-Ishar by Alfonso Archi, reflecting the reverence for the justice deity Ishar. Išhtup-Išar's reign is notable for the significant trade and cultural exchange between Mari and Ebla, with evidence of diplomatic correspondence and economic cooperation. He also oversaw the construction of the temple dedicated to Ishar, a testament to the importance of the deity in Mariote society. Išhtup-Išar's legacy extends to the Neo-Assyrian Empire, which would later adopt similar trade and diplomatic practices. The Mariote king's reign serves as a pivotal moment in the development of the Mariote kingdom, highlighting the complexities of regional politics and cultural exchange in ancient Mesopotamia. Ishar's enduring influence can be seen in the subsequent veneration of the deity in various ancient Near Eastern cultures, underscoring the significance of Išhtup-Išar's reign in shaping the regional trajectory of human civilization.

entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Išhtup-Išar (Ishtup-Ishar) was a king (lugal) of Mari in the second Mariote kingdom of the early Bronze Age, known from cuneiform sources that preserve his theophoric name linked to the justice deity Ishar. Rulers of Mari controlled a crucial Euphrates bend node between Syria and southern Mesopotamia.

His reign belongs to the era when Mari’s palace economy and diplomatic correspondence made the city a hinge of Amorite and pre-Amorite politics. Name readings (Išhtup-šar vs Ishtup-Ishar) track advances in onomastics and the cultic landscape of Mari and Ebla.

Išhtup-Išar is a Prosopographic anchor in early Mari’s royal sequence.
